projectDescription: An open-access agrometeorological and financial viability platform that uses ERA5 climate reanalysis, FAO-56 soil water balance, and XGBoost machine learning to evaluate white maize sowing viability in Calderas, San José Acatempa, Jutiapa, Guatemala.
keyFeatures: ERA5 satellite reanalysis data ingestion from 1981 to present (Open-Meteo Archive API)
FAO-56 continuous soil water balance simulation (Saxton & Rawls pedotransfer equations)
XGBoost and Logistic Regression ensemble with temporal GroupKFold cross-validation
Calibrated probability output with Brier Skill Score validation against local climatology
Tri-color agrometeorological traffic light (Green / Yellow / Red) for sowing decisions
ENSO phase detection (El Niño / La Niña / Neutral) via NOAA PSL MEI v2
120-day phenological rain streak analysis with canícula (dry spell) detection
Geometric terrain modeling for rectangular, triangular, and irregular quadrilateral parcels
Dynamic sowing density recommendations (5.8, 4.4, or 3.6 plants/m²) based on risk level
Real-time MAGA wholesale maize price scraper (La Terminal market, Guatemala City)
Full P&L financial projection with ROI, break-even, and three-scenario sensitivity analysis
Structured PDF report export with interactive browser viewer
Input hardening against SQL injection, XSS, and path traversal attacks
Strict geographic restriction to Calderas, San José Acatempa, Jutiapa bounding box
